svg.title: The cycle
svg.desc: A graph with two boxes. On the left a box labelled lock_a, with the address c1a4e0a0 and the words one lock class under it, and on the right the same for lock_b at c1a4e060. A solid arrow runs from lock_a to lock_b, labelled edge one, recorded when the first thread held lock_a and took lock_b. A dashed arrow runs back from lock_b to lock_a, labelled edge two, about to be recorded because the second thread holds lock_b and is taking lock_a. A note by the dashed arrow says it has not been added and that this is the moment lockdep says no. Underneath, three notes say what an edge means, that a loop means there is an order in which two of these block forever, and that nothing here is blocked because both threads finished.

text.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Two locks, two edges, one loop

text.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Lockdep works on a graph of lock classes rather than on a picture of stuck threads.

svg.text: Nothing is blocked here. No thread waited on anything. Both threads finished.

svg.text: The bug is in the code either way, and the graph is what says so.
